spec.name: selfcall-single-nonoverloaded-runtime-underflow

panel.evidence: Step 2 calls h(250), which computes this.f(250) = 250-200 = 50 with no arithmetic underflow under Solidity 0.8 checked math; EVM dry-run and committed status are 'success' with storage {direct: 50} (nonzero_entries=1, value '50'). Polkadot dry-run returns status 'error' with a large nested DispatchError-style blob (multiple repeated account-id patterns '8eaf0415...4794f26a48', indicating nested call frames) and the committed tx reverts, leaving storage count 0. Step 1 g(0) shows no divergence, so both chains revert the genuine underflow 0-200 identically; the divergence is isolated to a semantically well-defined succeeding self-call. No env-value source markers (gasleft/block.*/tx.*) are present and gas comparison is disabled, so the documented known differences do not apply. The storage-count mismatch is downstream of the revert (direct never written), not an independent packing/endianness artifact.
panel.rationale: An external self-call this.f(x) with no underflow reverting on pallet-contracts while succeeding on EVM points at a real semantic defect in solang's substrate external-call dispatch/revert propagation for self-calls, possibly triggered by state after the prior reverted self-call in step 1; the nested-frame error blob supports failure inside the internal call plumbing rather than in the arithmetic. This is not the historical contract-type-name call issue (#1007/PR #1011, which concerned Base.f() and was fixed) nor the large-constant arithmetic bug #1507. I cannot fully decode the revert blob, and cross-transaction state carryover via the harness is a possible alternative explanation, so confidence is medium rather than high; a minimal repro isolating h(250) without the prior g(0) revert would confirm.
panel.cluster_hint: solang substrate external self-call (this.f) reverts at runtime for non-underflowing input; suspect self-call dispatch/revert propagation after a prior reverted self-call

panel.evidence: Step 2 calls h(250), which computes this.f(250) = 250 - 200 = 50 with no underflow; EVM commits successfully and storage count shows 1 nonzero entry with value 50, while Polkadot dry-run returns an error and the committed tx reverts, leaving 0 nonzero entries. The revert blob contains a nested module error (repeating '010308160000...' inside the outer '030816000000...' payload with embedded account IDs), indicating the inner external self-call itself trapped/failed and propagated. The underflow case (g(0), step 0) matched on both chains, so the divergence is specifically the non-underflowing external self-call h(250).
panel.rationale: Solidity semantics for h(250) are unambiguous: this.f(250) = 50, assignment to `direct` must succeed, matching solc/anvil exactly. The revert is not explained by intentional chain differences (no env values or gas involved; gas oracle off, no value transfer), and the storage mismatch reflects the revert rather than a count-mode packing/endianness artifact since the EVM side holds a single uint256 value 50. The pattern points at solang's substrate-target lowering of `this.f(x)` external self-calls (dispatch/reentrancy/return-data handling) trapping at runtime. Historical record #1007/#1011 concerns calls via contract type name (a compile-time issue), not runtime self-calls, so it is not a match; the nested-error blob suggests the inner call failed independently of the outer frame.
panel.cluster_hint: external self-call via `this.f(x)` reverts on Polkadot for a non-underflowing input; nested module error propagates from the inner self-call

adversarial.evidence: The divergent step (h(250)) is semantically unambiguous under Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic: this.f(250)=50 cannot underflow, there is no value transfer or access control, and EVM dry-run and committed status both succeed with storage {direct:50}. The control step g(0) exercises the same external self-call path with a genuine underflow and matches on both chains (both revert), isolating the defect to the succeeding self-call rather than to arithmetic or setup. The documented known differences do not apply: no env-value source markers (gasleft/block.*/tx.*) appear in the source, gas comparison is disabled, and the primary divergence is STATUS/TX_STATUS — not a storage-count artifact (the storage count 0 vs 1 is fully explained by the revert, and the EVM side holds a single plain uint256, ruling out packing/endianness count-mode noise). The revert blob contains a nested dispatch-style error with repeated embedded account IDs, consistent with failure inside nested call-frame plumbing rather than an outer-frame oracle failure, and it appears in both dry-run and committed forms, so it is not a dry-run-only oracle artifact. Historical records do not match: #1007/PR #1011 is a compile-time issue for calls via contract type name (Base.f), fixed; #1507 concerns large-constant multiplication (>=0x200000001), not a small checked subtraction; the span/Snyk records are irrelevant.
adversarial.rationale: Every documented known difference and every historical record fails to explain a successful, value-free, non-underflowing external self-call reverting on pallet-contracts while succeeding on EVM, with a matched underflow control case on the same code path. The strongest remaining counter-hypothesis — cross-transaction state carryover in the harness from the reverted step-1 call — is speculative, would itself be an undocumented harness defect, and is testable with a minimal repro of h(250) in isolation; it does not reclassify the finding, only bounds confidence at medium. The evidence survives scrutiny as a genuine solang substrate-target self-call dispatch/revert-propagation defect candidate.

screening.cluster_hint: solang substrate external self-call (this.f) reverts at runtime for non-underflowing input; suspect self-call dispatch/revert propagation after a prior reverted self-call

history.title: Add Rename functionality
history.text:
This feature depends on having the right span information for identifiers in the parse tree. Currently, some changes are needed to either add the missing span information in some cases, or improve the already present spans (look for one-off errors). 

The rest of the "goto-*" functions also depend on the availability of proper spans. But in their case, as no modification is made to the source code, lack of accurate spans is less of an issue. But `rename` does modify the source code and hence having incorrect spans can result in unintentionally overwriting pieces of source code, which is highly undesirable. 

The changes made as part of this PR provide the necessary code for `rename` to work. Correcting the parse tree is expected to be done as part of future PRs

A non-exhaustive list of changes to be made to parse tree:  (https://github.com/hyperledger/solang/pull/1411#issuecomment-1648031602)

1. No loc for contract variables type - array_type_dynamic_push.sol L6
2. No loc for constructor base call - abstract_contract_inheritance.sol L14
3. No loc for function modifier arguments - function_modifier_arguments.sol L8
4. No loc for function override base contracts - virtua
